notes.title: Major Update Behind the Scenes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/5ec6261d9018c708bf34dd56a659198bbb9049bf.png[/img]
Hello everyone!

Already in 2025! Wow, time flies, especially when you're playing Sneak In!
I received feedback from a player who should thank her husband, as he contacted me about a bug in Sneak In.

Level 145 was causing the game to crash on Windows. And on Windows only, on Mac or Linux everything was working fine.
Anyway, I was already working on optimizations, so I took the opportunity to look into this crash.

It took me a good 30 minutes to reproduce the bug, and 2 hours to understand it. After that, everything went quite quickly, as the bug is no longer present.
And as a bonus, with this version 3, there's more stability, since the log management has been revised, but also a major optimization that allows Sneak In to run on really low-powered computers.

I rewrote the algorithms that were responsible for managing marble collisions, and it has clearly improved performance.

That's all from me, it's a huge update since all the code has changed, even if visually nothing seems to have moved.

Thanks for reading
Enjoy the game
Xavier aka Binogure

notes.title: Better steam integration and crash fix
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/5ec6261d9018c708bf34dd56a659198bbb9049bf.png[/img]
Hey folks!

It's been too long, folks! Like 2024 snapped, and here we are in 2025!
Anyway, this new update brings a new world to all of you!

A better Steam integration, meaning the game won't close if it doesn't detect Steam the first time. It will keep trying for at least 2 minutes with a 10-second interval. And afterwards, it's going to close itself.

Another couple of fixes. It might happen from time to time that the game crashes randomly while playing, which is really annoying. I fixed 3 of those crashes. The first one was due to a deadlock of the log file. When the game gets an error, it writes into a log file. But if it cannot write into the log file, then it raises another error and eventually tries to write into a log file... but again it raises another error, and the error handler tries to write into a log file... I think you get it now.

I added 2 guard clauses to prevent it from happening. First, the log gets disabled if it cannot write, meaning no more error loop. The other guard clause postpones the error handler to another frame, giving Windows more time to recover and eventually store data.

Anyway, the other patch is for the log file too, but when the game tries to make a dump of the log file, if it can't do it, it no longer crashes. And the last one is to disable low-end motherboard manufacturer hot patches that lead to instability and random crashes.

That's it folks, I hope you like this better version of Sneak In.
By the way, both the game and the demo got those upgrades!

Happy new year and best wishes!
Xavier aka Binogure

Unique worlds are waiting for you. Thirty new levels to challenge you!

I have plans to add in-game achievements. So when you unlock an achievement, an animation plays in Sneak In. And other animations are going to be added to enhance your gaming experience.

For March, you had 30 new levels, I hope to keep up the pace and provide you with as many each month. If all goes well, this will bring us to 240 levels by the end of the summer!

That's it for today.
Thanks for reading, and go enjoy Sneak In

notes.title: A new world
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/9ee0691cdb8fc9267cfac2464f8eb38dabb83569.png[/img]
Good morning friends!

I wish you all well! It's already February and as promised here is the sixth world of Sneak In! 15 new levels and some changes, let's talk about it now!

[h2]The survival mode[/h2]
This mode that never ends has been slightly revised. Indeed, when you launch the infinite mode, you get 3 bonuses of each. The bonuses you earn in endless mode are lost once the game is over. Make sure you use them quickly, you'll always get as many bonuses when you restart the game anyway!

[h2]Other changes[/h2]
Upon launching a level, there is a pop-up that lists which marbles will be present. This list of images used to be small and hard to read on small screens. In v2.2.0, all of the marbles in the display panel have been enlarged, and the marbles are now easily distinguishable.

Some of you pointed out that changing the position of the cannon by clicking on it could be cumbersome on heavy levels and suggested that you could change the position of the cannon by pressing a key. Thus, you can switch the position of the cannon by pressing the space key on your keyboard. That's very convenient.

One more change. In case you consume bonuses during a level but you lose, or you close your game, then the bonuses that were consumed will be returned to you. This is more fair play, and it's a suggestion from Bulobon, so thank him!

As for the fix, Steam achievements should work properly from now on!

That's it for today, see you next month for another new world!
Good day to all

Xavier aka Binogure

notes.title: Revamp is NOW!
notes.content:
Hey folks!

We finally have a new version of Sneak In, and I'm excited to announce it!
Well, today we're going to talk about the key changes as well as what's coming up for you in the next few months!

[h2]What is new?[/h2]
Almost everything has changed since then. It progresses from the cannon that launches the marbles to the snake at the level's end, through all of the marbles, and finally, all of the levels have been redesigned. The main menu and the world map are the only things that haven't changed. Even so, both have been modified. For example, the world map has a cleaner path and more evenly distributed leaves.

Concerning the gameplay, it is required to earn a certain number of points to clear a level, and you will be awarded a badge according to the time it took you to complete the level. The faster you finish it, the better the medal.

Some stages feature one or more marble tracks. There are also moving walls and other juicy effects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/3513a4954a50b63777fc4bcbf5e63c8d09c81e3a.gif[/img]

[h2]Upcoming updates?[/h2]
As you may have noticed, Sneak In doesn't have as many levels as before. However, the 60 levels of the game look better and feel more balanced. Over time, I plan to add new levels until it reaches 250 levels. Thus upcoming updates are going to contain both patches and more content as well.

Please feel free to share your suggestions with me on Steam, or come and talk about them on the studio's Discord server.

Happy holidays to all.
Binogure

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/b748c8bcb70af0b99f661389e54b782fda2738bd.gif[/img]

Also, I found out that the main menu was too static, so I added a fog effect and re-exported most of the assets in 1440p, so the game looks better on larger resolution.
Discord rich presence has also been added.

That's all folks!
I hope you enjoy Sneak In!
Binogure

notes.title: Sneak In is OUT!
notes.content:
Hello people!

TL;DR: Sneak In is a Zuma style match-3 game, with more than 200 levels, 7 special marbles, 3 different bonuses, a world map that I hope you will enjoy and an infinite level where you can spend all the time you want.

[h2]Backstory[/h2]
I've been working alone on Binogure Studio for 3 years now. Before that I was already working in video games, but for other companies. And 3 years ago I gave up everything to start developing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/726840/City_Game_Studio/]City Game Studio[/url]. After a few months of development, I realize that the City Game Studio project is too big. Not think twice, I I start working on Sneak In. I wanted it to be a mobile game without ads or tracking feature. 6 months later, and after [url=https://godotengine.org/article/godot-3-0-released]several contributions to Godot Engine[/url], Sneak In is published for mobile and hardly has found its audience. Although the reviews are very positive, Sneak In, [url=https://godotengine.org/article/godot-3-0-released]like the vast majority of mobile games[/url], falls into oblivion.

Sneak In is a commercial failure, but a professional success. Publishing Sneak In has taught me a lot about the development process, marketing and account management.

[h2]What's new?[/h2]
This version has no life, which means you can play as long as you want. The visual effects have been redesigned and there is the possibility, by right clicking, to change the colour of the marble you will shoot. These are differences that may seem subtle but that deeply change the gameplay (and make the game even more fun).
Assets have been exported in high resolution, music and sound effects exported in much better quality. In addition, the Steam version supports Remote Play on phone and tablet.
So you will be able to play on PC, tablet and mobile phone at the same time.

[h2]Closing words[/h2]
I spent 6 months making Sneak In, and 2 months promoting it on the Internet. This is a small project that should bring you complete satisfaction.

Thanks to all of you,
Binogure

notes.title: Welcome to the chicahua jungle
notes.content:
Hello fellow casual gamers,

Sneak In is the first game I released. Back in 2017, I worried about failing the release of City Game Studio (CGS has been released in 2019). I read several gamasutra's articles explaining that the first game you might want to release should be a little game. In the indie gaming industry, it means ~6 months of development. The reason is simple, when you release your first game, you will learn a lot by making mistakes. So I started working on a second tiny project.

And since Zuma is my favorite of the match-3 games genre, I started working on a neo-Zuma game with a twist.

[h2]Unique world map[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/8049b8c545ff8b3772740a4ade500e2bd8070a35.gif[/img]
I wanted to make a world map that you want to explore. By scrolling, it will play cute animations, and you can spend time playing with the world map. Since I lived in Montreal, I started walking in the city looking for mural painting. I took a lot of pictures and made a mood board. 2 months later, the worldmap of Sneak In was made. There are 16 animations, one per world.

[h2]Bonuses[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/dd5928d79314fe8527f4760905be3a551ad9dfa4.gif[/img]
Did I mention that I wanted to make a neo-Zuma game? It is quite ambitious since I spent hundreds of hour playing Zuma, and thousands playing other marble shooter games. Sneak In is my answer to the plethora of marble shooter games all alike. Every world has 14 levels plus 1 hard-level. Everytime you beat a world, you get a bonus. There are 3 bonuses in Sneak In, and you can use them when you need them. A bomb, a marble matcher and a time machine. 

[h2]Marble with special powers[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/06e97334aaa37d464d7d6149a684fa311038f8ab.gif[/img]
There are 7 magic marbles: The frozen, the bumpies, the ghosts, the rocks, the bubbles, the viruses and the blackholes. The frozen needs to explode 4 times before melting. The bumpies act as wall, and shooting one 3 times make it round, and it acts as a normal marble. A red ghosts marbles needs to be shot with a red marble to melt. There are green, yellow, purple, brown, blue ghost marbles. A rock can be paint with any other marble. A bubble marble matches with any other marble (those are my favorite). The virus marbles are killed when a marble explode near them and the blackholes marbles need to be shot several times before melting.

[h2]Still missing something[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34817774/d35fd65dee401ce2738cec6394555bec417f370e.gif[/img]
I enjoy playing marble shooters, so I made 240 levels, but once you've done with them, you've pretty much finished the game. Which is great, but you might still want to play it from time to time. So I made an infinite level that changes every week, and there is a worldwide leaderboard.

A demo will be available next week and I hope that, like me you will like Sneak In!
Thank you for reading me.

Regards
Binogure
